match_id: EDWARDS: “FINAL NAIL IN THE COFFIN!”  Wolves_Tottenham_2026-04-25_ed4kM-cHfRg
team: EDWARDS: “FINAL NAIL IN THE COFFIN!”  Wolves
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
The pressure was very much on Spurs today  and they very much needed a win for them.  
How do you initially sum up that, Rob?  
Not much in the game. I thought they edged  the first half but I didn't feel under threat.  
I thought we had more of the second half  and there was nothing really in the game.  
In the end, the way it was going to go, it was  going to be a moment of magic or a second phase  
of a set piece, something like that, that won  it, which obviously proved to be the case. Boos  
towards the end as well. I imagine you can sense  the frustration during the game. The frustration,  
yeah, of course. We're bottom of the  league. We've just lost three in a row,  
so it's not as easy as turn up and just beat  Tottenham because they've been having a bad  
time. They've got a lot of good players and their  motivation level was incredibly high. It might  
sound weird to you all, I don't know if you really  fully appreciate what I'm saying, but it's been  
really challenging this week for us. We've been  officially relegated. It's been really tough. So  
for the players to give everything and  match their intensity and match Tottenham's  
levels of work rate, the lads deserve a lot  of credit for that. In the end, we lacked  
a little bit of cutting edge, which we know where  we're at at the moment. So that's the situation.  
Hi Rob. With those boos at the end and the flag  that went up, that relationship with supporters  
and the wider club, is that something that you  believe can be mended? Because it's been really  
strained for quite a bit. I hope so. I thought  they were brilliant throughout the whole game,  
the supporters. I've not got a negative word to  say about them at all. Like I said, we've lost  
three in a row. We're bottom of the league. We've  been relegated this week. They're not going to be  
happy. They're not going to be happy. But what  I need everyone to understand is that everyone's  
giving their all. Everyone is giving their all and  it is going to take some time to turn this around.  
We're not in the middle of a transfer window  now. We can't change loads. We're trying. We've  
improved from the last week. We looked a lot more  solid today. We didn't give a lot away at all,  
but we are where we are. We are where we are.  We're working really really hard to try and  
put things right, and in a few weeks' time we'll  be able to action a lot of that stuff as well.  
In terms of mending that relationship I talked  about, I mean it didn't really make sense in the  
press conference room, but I suppose it's more  actions than words. Is that fair? Yeah, we have.  
Yeah, we have, and we all know that. Yeah, we  know that. That's no problem at the moment.  
Yeah, times are tough. We've  got to stand up, take it,  
and then hopefully in a year's time we're sitting  in a much more positive place. You also gave  
Lima an opportunity today. Was that very much  with an eye on next season? It was with an eye  
on winning the game today. They deserved it, I  thought. Actually they performed really well.  
We knew we needed a lot of legs today.  Tottenham run hard. Like I said before,  
their motivation levels are incredibly  high. Roberto De Zerbi's come in, who has  
loads of energy and everything as well. We had to  be able to match that. So with the lads that came  
into the team, it wasn't purely with a view of  next year. It was to try and win the game today.  
And we tried to push. That was why we put Tolu on  with however many minutes to go. We don't want to  
go with another striker, but we tried to push. We  felt like we were in the ascendancy in that second  
half, which we were. I realise you can't change  the situation, but it kind of feels like you can't  
be gaining a great deal from the remaining  games. I guess you probably quite see and do it.  
You can if you win four games in a row, but  obviously we can't just do that. There's obviously  
a lot more to it than just turning up and winning  the games. We know the level we're at as well.  
I know what you're saying and I get it, but  the situation is there's four more games left  
and we've got to make sure that we turn up and we  fight. And again, I looked around the room at the  
very end and went around every single one of them.  There's not one there I could say gave up, didn't  
try, not one of them. They gave their all today.  Okay, we were lacking in one or two bits, but  
there was nothing in it. There was nothing in  the game. So it wasn't effort or anyone giving  
up or downing tools. We've got to make sure  that we continue that for the next four games.  
On João Gomes, there's been obviously talk about  interest in him behind the scenes. Is it a player  
you're sort of resigned to losing? There'll  certainly be interest in João and I get it,  
he's a phenomenal player. But I think, again, you  saw from his commitment out there today and his  
performance level that whatever's going on off the  pitch, it won't affect him. Actually, just on that  
very quickly as well, he seemed quite animated and  fired up today, and I say that in a positive way.  
Has that conversation been with you during the  game as well? They were. I thought the lads were.  
Yeah, it's hard because people don't want to hear  it after we've lost, but there were some really  
good performances there today and there's a real  commitment from all of them. There really was.  
They really really tried. They're with  it. They're with us. They're fighting.  
They really are. It's been hard this week. Final  nail in the coffin, relegated. Maybe other teams  
would have just gone under completely today and  it might have been an absolute shambles. It wasn't  
that. It was a proper game of football, but we've  lost it. So people will say what they want to say  
about that, that's fine. But no, those boys that  were out there today gave everything. Thank you.
title: EDWARDS: “FINAL NAIL IN THE COFFIN!”  Wolves 0-1 Tottenham
